title: Fair play
step1: 1. Before each hand your phone picks a secret, and so does every other player. The table server adds a fifth secret of its own and picks the bots' secrets.
step2: 2. All five SHA-256 fingerprints are published before anyone reveals. Your phone only reveals its secret once it holds all five, so no one can pick a secret after seeing yours. The shuffle seed is the hash of all five secrets together.
step3: 3. When the hand ends, the secrets, any restarts of the deal and the full action log are published. Your phone checks the fingerprints, re-derives the seed, replays the hand, and checks the log against every move it sent, every table state it was shown and every move the table made for you.
step4: 4. Hands are checked as a chain. Each hand must start from the scores, dealer and wind the last one left, no hand can be skipped or dealt twice, and the final scores are accepted only when the hands your phone verified lead to them. The table may move for you only once your turn clock and time bank, as the table rules set them, have run out, and it may not turn away a move that was legal.
partialLabel: Logged — the server could have picked this deal
partialAfter: passed every check, but your phone cannot rule out that the server chose its deal, or did not watch all of it: the server made your secret for you (you were late or away), you joined mid-hand, the deal was restarted, your connection dropped while the deal was being agreed, the hand was played while you were away, or the app or the server restarted around it. Only a hand marked Verified had a deal your phone watched from start to finish in one attempt.
trust: What no phone can check: the server knows the seed when it deals, so it sees every wall and could look at it during the hand or leak it to a player. It is trusted not to. To limit the damage a leak could do, each account gets only one seat per table, and quick match never seats players who have blocked each other. There is no "luck balancing", no streak engine, no hidden weights. The engine is deterministic and open; the only randomness is the seed above.
endUnverified: The match is over, but your phone could not check the final scores: it does not hold an unbroken record of this match's hands.

caveat.standIn: The server made this seat's secret (it was late or away), so it could have picked this deal.
caveat.joined: You joined during this hand: its log checked out, but your secret was not part of the deal.
caveat.restarted: The deal was restarted, so the server could have picked which attempt to keep.
caveat.linkLost: Your connection dropped while the deal was being agreed, so your phone did not watch all of it.
caveat.missedAttempts: Your phone did not see every attempt at this deal.
caveat.away: Your phone was away when this hand ended. It checked the hand's record afterwards, but did not watch the play.
caveat.gap: Your phone missed the hands before this one and was not shown their records, so it could not check the scores this hand started from.
caveat.serverRestart: The server restarted during this hand, and some turns were played again.
caveat.appRestart: The app was restarted around this deal, so your phone cannot be sure it watched all of it. This is expected for the first hand after a restart; later hands can be Verified again.

failure.dealtPlayedHand: The table tried to deal a hand that had already been played.
failure.startedBeforeEnd: The table started a new hand before the current one had finished.
failure.dealtAfterMatch: The table dealt another hand after the match was over.
failure.dealtOutOfTurn: The table dealt a hand out of order.
failure.matchStartChanged: The match did not start the way a new match must: the scores, the dealer or the round wind had been changed.
failure.handStartChanged: This hand did not start where the last one ended: the scores, the dealer or the round wind were different.
failure.botsChanged: The table changed which seats are bots during the match.
failure.movedMatch: The table moved you into a different match partway through.
failure.movedSeat: The table moved you to a different seat partway through the match.
failure.rulesChanged: The table changed the rules partway through the match.
failure.redealt: The table dealt this hand again while it was being played.
failure.wentBack: The table went back to a hand that had already finished.
failure.resentOtherMatch: The table sent a finished hand again, this time as part of a different match.
failure.auditChanged: The table sent a different record for a hand that had already finished.
failure.resultChanged: The table sent a different result for a hand that had already finished.
failure.endUnsupported: The table announced the end of the match, but the hands your phone checked do not lead to it.
failure.twoStates: The table showed your phone two different versions of the table at turn %{turn}.

failure.missedWhileConnected: The table said your phone missed a hand, although it was connected the whole time.

failure.commitsChanged: The table changed the fingerprints after publishing them.
failure.myCommitDiffers: The table published a fingerprint for your seat that is not the one your phone sent.
failure.earlyReveal: The table asked for your secret before it had published all five fingerprints.
failure.neverAskedToCommit: The table never asked your phone to take part in this deal.
failure.commitsNeverArrived: The fingerprints for this deal never reached your phone.
failure.noContext: Your phone has no match to check this hand against.
failure.auditMalformed: The record of this hand is damaged.

failure.moveInvented: The record shows a move you never made (turn %{turn}).

failure.moveIgnored: The table ignored a move you sent in good time and played its own instead (turn %{turn}).

failure.attemptsBelowSeen: The record counts the attempts at the deal as %{attempts}, but your phone took part in attempt %{seen}.
failure.attemptsNotSeen: The record counts the attempts at the deal as %{attempts}, but your phone counted %{times}.
failure.restartBlamesNoOne: Restart %{n} of the deal blames no seat, yet your phone saw every attempt without losing its connection.
failure.restartBlamesMeStoodIn: Restart %{n} of the deal blames your seat, although the server had already made your secret for you.
failure.restartBlamesMeRevealed: Restart %{n} of the deal blames your seat although your phone had revealed its secret, and the table then asked it for a new secret instead of making one for you.
failure.blamedButUsed: The record blames your seat for a restart of the deal, yet the deal used a new secret from your phone instead of one the server made for you.
